evidence_against: A premature late-cycle bearish interpretation is challenged by the short-horizon data: BTC returned +0.06% and ETH +0.06% over 1h; ETH was also +0.05% over 4h, while ETH/BTC rose +0.13% over 4h and +0.26% over 12h.

Direct ETH/BTC hourly closes remained above 0.0300 throughout the supplied 168-hour sample. This does not confirm renewed leadership, but it contradicts a claim of a confirmed break below that observed level.

Longer-horizon rotation context is not uniformly weak: the supplied BlockchainCenter 30d and 90d scores are both 55, with 27 of 49 constituents outperforming BTC; the separate CMC 90d published score is 62. Method disagreement limits interpretation, but these readings do not support a one-sided broad-rotation-collapse conclusion.

BTC and ETH positioning signals differ by horizon: BTC/ETH OI fell over 12h but rose over 24h and 72h; BTC funding is slightly positive while ETH funding is slightly negative. These observations do not establish a singular leverage-driven deterioration mechanism.
evidence_for: The strongest coherent deterioration reading is the alignment of negative 24h and 72h returns: BTC is -2.54% and -3.79%, ETH is -4.49% and -5.63%, and ETH/BTC is -2.00% and -1.90%, respectively. ETH underperformed BTC over both horizons.

Both supplied breadth proxies are severely negative at their respective snapshots: the latest top-100 proxy shows 12 advancers versus 86 decliners, and the rich-breadth proxy reports a 10% advance ratio, 10 advancers, and a -3.45% equal-weight 24h return. They remain proxy-only evidence.

Aggressive quote flow is negative for BTC and ETH across every supplied 1h, 4h, 12h, 24h, and 72h horizon. Mean taker-buy quote shares are below 0.5 throughout these windows, including 0.48/0.41 for BTC/ETH over 24h and 0.48/0.45 over 72h.
Sentiment weakened during the capture sequence: CFGI is Fear for BTC (34), ETH (23), and the market (37), with BTC and ETH scores down from the predecessor capture.

The conflict router records multi-horizon and breadth-cross conflicts, including positive short-horizon return/OI observations against negative intermediate and longer-horizon return observations. Thus, the evidence supports fragility and disagreement rather than a resolved directional regime.
hypotheses: Most coherent interpretation: the supplied data are consistent with a broader pullback or deterioration phase that has produced an early, fragile stabilization attempt. The negative 24h/72h price performance, weak proxy breadth, negative aggressive flow, Fear readings, and ETH-relative weakness are mutually reinforcing; the positive 1h/parts of the 4h data are insufficient on their own to establish reversal.

Strongest falsification of that interpretation: the short-horizon improvement represents recovery rather than a transient bounce. This would be supported, but is not currently established, by sustained positive returns beyond the 1h/4h windows together with improved breadth and participation, stabilizing or strengthening ETH/BTC, and less negative flow.

Premature late-cycle bearishness is specifically challenged because the evidence does not show a confirmed distribution sequence: direct ETH/BTC has remained above 0.0300 in the observed sample, medium-horizon rotation scores are mixed-to-moderate rather than uniformly weak, and leverage observations change sign across horizons.

Delayed recognition of genuine deterioration remains a competing risk because a short-lived uptick can coexist with materially negative 24h/72h performance, poor proxy breadth, and persistent negative aggressive flow. The supplied evidence cannot determine whether the short-horizon move will persist.
summary: Conflict review only: the detected disagreement is best described as fragile short-horizon stabilization within an unresolved broader deterioration signal. The strongest bearish-coherent case comes from aligned negative 24h/72h BTC, ETH, and ETH/BTC returns, very weak proxy breadth, and negative aggressive flow at all supplied horizons. The strongest falsification is that 1h/selected 4h recovery, 168-hour ETH/BTC persistence above 0.0300, and mixed medium-horizon rotation measures may develop into a broader recovery. Neither outcome is established; no canonical state, action, rule, or forecast is asserted.
uncertainties: Breadth observations are point-in-time proxy-only measures with changing membership and do not confirm canonical broad-alt or large-cap breadth.
Macro and Binance spot owners are disabled, so their unavailable evidence remains unknown.
The settled ETF rows are for 2026-10-06 and were retrieved roughly 11 hours before the cutoff; they do not confirm same-session transmission.
Pullback Forensics was observed after the stated decision cutoff and is shadow-only; it is not used as cutoff-time directional confirmation.
The persistence and breadth of the short-horizon bounce are unknown. The supplied data do not establish whether it is a reversal or a countertrend stabilization.
The action-compass calibration is descriptive, low-confidence in the displayed cohorts, and has no matured typed warning rows; it cannot validate a pullback, distribution, exit, or re-entry rule.
